canonical_title: Hidden in Plain Sight: Benchmarking Agent Safety Against Decomposition Attacks with DECOMPBENCH
mechanism_manipulated: Harmful intent is decomposed into independent benign-looking subtasks; conversation state is cleared between victim calls while environment state persists, bundling decomposition with context loss.
authoritative_policy_source: Provider/model refusal safeguards; benchmark checkpoints define global harmful completion; no executable application policy.
number_of_principals: 1 provider/safety principal plus 1 malicious user; fresh victim calls are not separate authority principals.
agents_or_models: One victim agent service invoked repeatedly through fresh sessions.
attacker_type: Black-box malicious user assisted by an LLM decomposer.
defender_visibility: Each victim call sees only its current subtask; no cross-call monitor; environment state persists.
multi_agent_causal_control: no: monolithic prompts are compared with multiple stateless calls, so prompt granularity and context retention both change; not a single-versus-multi-agent architecture control.
defense_evaluated: None evaluated; benchmark leaves defense development to future work.
conclusion_scope: mechanism-specific: independent-subtask decomposition under provider safeguards.
audit_notes: A multi-session decomposition study, not a genuine multi-agent causal comparison.

canonical_title: Context-Fractured Decomposition Attacks on Tool-Using LLM Agents: Exploiting Artifact Provenance Gaps
mechanism_manipulated: Semantic decomposition, cross-session memory fracture, and artifact-mediated transfer jointly exploit missing causal provenance.
authoritative_policy_source: System defense prompt and model safeguards locally; AgentDojo goals/artifacts and an offline evaluator define global harm.
number_of_principals: 1 benchmark/system policy principal plus 1 attacker; victim roles do not have distinct legitimate authority.
agents_or_models: Four victim-agent roles in the harness, including an optional advisor.
attacker_type: External malicious user whose unrestricted planner produces subgoals.
defender_visibility: Local monitor sees current prompt and immediate tool interaction but not artifact lineage; trace-omniscient evaluator sees full trace and artifacts.
multi_agent_causal_control: partial: memory/visibility variations and counterfactual probes are useful, but decomposition, context reset, artifact transfer, and topology are not isolated as one matched factor.
defense_evaluated: Strong local judge and trace-omniscient upper bound evaluated; provenance lineage tagging is proposed.
conclusion_scope: mechanism-specific: context fracture through artifact provenance gaps.
audit_notes: Do not interpret its attack success as a pure effect of agent count.

canonical_title: Jailbreak-as-a-Service++: Unveiling Distributed AI-Driven Malicious Information Campaigns Powered by LLM Crowdsourcing
mechanism_manipulated: Counterfactual task mapping, semantic decomposition/unit toxification, and scheduling across heterogeneous providers bundle decomposition, heterogeneity, and information isolation.
authoritative_policy_source: Each provider's independent safety policy; ALERT/MHS tasks and an evaluator define campaign success; no shared authoritative policy.
number_of_principals: Multiple provider principals; main workflow uses 3 model roles and governance simulation models 5 providers; 1 centralized adversary.
agents_or_models: Three model roles in the main workflow; multiple models/providers in experiments.
attacker_type: Malicious user/scheduler using multiple models, accounts, or providers.
defender_visibility: Each provider normally sees its own requests/accounts; simulations vary local, regional, or global fingerprint sharing and guardrail strength.
multi_agent_causal_control: partial: ablations and individual-model comparisons are informative, but decomposition, model heterogeneity, and provider isolation remain bundled.
defense_evaluated: Simulated fingerprint sharing, probabilistic provider guardrails, account banning/cross-provider coordination, and detection.
conclusion_scope: scoped generalization: distributed cross-provider crowdsourcing, not every local-allow/global-harm mechanism.
audit_notes: PoisonSwarm is the framework name, not the canonical paper title.

canonical_title: Beyond Single-Agent Alignment: Preventing Context-Fragmented Violations in Multi-Agent Systems
mechanism_manipulated: Organization-wide policy facts are split across private domain graphs, allowing cross-domain semantic laundering or violation without any one agent seeing the whole invariant.
authoritative_policy_source: Author-defined organizational invariants backed by a structured registry and authorization matrix.
number_of_principals: 1 organization-level policy principal; policy facts are distributed across 17 agents in 7 domains.
agents_or_models: 17 agents across 7 organizational domains in PhantomEcosystem.
attacker_type: Primarily structural/benign over-compliance; threat discussion also permits malicious or colluding participants.
defender_visibility: Each agent sees its domain model; sidecars mediate messages/tool calls, exchange signed metadata, and issue boolean cross-domain policy queries; a central checker is the stronger reference.
multi_agent_causal_control: partial: cross-domain/same-domain cases and centralized checks help, but there is no clean randomized single-agent/full-policy versus fragmented multi-agent contrast for the same workflow.
defense_evaluated: Distributed Sentinel; prompt firewall, rule DLP, partial monolithic sentinel, LLM judge, and central policy checker baselines.
conclusion_scope: scoped generalization: distributed organizational workflows with private policy fragments and mediated communication.
audit_notes: Strongly relevant multi-agent paper, but causal isolation of fragmentation is incomplete.

canonical_title: MasDrift: Benchmarking Authorization Preservation Across Multi-Agent Architectures
mechanism_manipulated: Authorization and constraints drift as a request is delegated through centralized or decentralized coordination topologies.
authoritative_policy_source: Original user's request and task-specific critical constraint/reserved actions.
agents_or_models: Single agent or centralized/decentralized structures with up to 8 agents.
attacker_type: None in the primary benchmark; violations arise from ordinary coordination and over-completion.
defender_visibility: Source anchoring sees original request, public tool surface, and pending call; chain enforcement sees carried parent policy and delegated subtask; offline scoring sees complete trace.
multi_agent_causal_control: yes: same 600 tasks and tools are run under single-agent and centralized/decentralized multi-agent topologies; count, depth, handoffs, and tool exposure still co-vary within scaling.
defense_evaluated: Source-anchored reference monitor and monotone authorization-carrying chain compared with no defense.
conclusion_scope: scoped generalization: authorization preservation and architecture-induced drift; strongest architecture-level causal evidence in this set.
audit_notes: Closest methodological precedent for a controlled single-agent versus multi-agent comparison.

canonical_title: ChainCaps: Composition-Safe Tool-Using Agents via Monotonic Capability Attenuation
mechanism_manipulated: Explicit data is permission-laundered through individually allowed source, transform, and sink tool calls.
authoritative_policy_source: Deployment-operator manifests assigning source budgets, sink privileges, and pass-through rules.
number_of_principals: 1 deployment policy principal and 1 tool-using agent; tools are resources, not policy principals.
attacker_type: Direct or indirect prompt injector controlling prompts, retrieved content, or tool output; benign workflows can also create risky flow.
defender_visibility: Transparent MCP proxy sees mediated tool calls/results, source identities, sinks, and explicit data flow; not covert channels, hidden model state, OS effects, or bypassed tools.
multi_agent_causal_control: no: with/without-defense runs use single tool-using agents; no matched single-versus-multi-agent comparison.
defense_evaluated: Monotonic sink-specific capability attenuation, lineage, explicit declassification, and fail-closed enforcement; compared with modeled scalar IFC/PFI alternatives.
conclusion_scope: mechanism-specific: operator-modeled proxy-visible explicit data flow under trusted manifests.
audit_notes: Relevant defense architecture, but not empirical evidence about multi-agent causation.

canonical_title: AgentFlow: A Flow-Centric Policy Language and Framework for Securing LLM Agent Systems
mechanism_manipulated: No single mechanism isolated; framework models policy-visible paths involving tainted data, trust laundering, malicious tools, and delegated or compromised agents.
authoritative_policy_source: Application/deployment operator's declarative flow policy plus user task scope.
number_of_principals: Not fixed; typically 1 operator/application principal plus a user delegator, with optional subagents and tools.
attacker_type: Indirect prompt injector, malicious tool provider, or compromised subagent.
defender_visibility: Trusted reference monitor observes mediated tool calls, delegation, modeled response sinks, provenance/taint, and session paths; unmediated paths/covert channels are outside scope.
multi_agent_causal_control: no: evaluation compares framework conditions on agent benchmarks/replays; optional delegation is modeled but agent multiplicity is not isolated.
defense_evaluated: Declarative flow/path rules, task-scoped capabilities, runtime taint/provenance enforcement, and bounded SMT verification.
conclusion_scope: scoped generalization: configured mediated policy-visible flows, not all unsafe behavior.
audit_notes: Useful policy and enforcement substrate rather than an isolated causal study.

canonical_title: Operational Reframing and Approval-Framed Delegation in Multi-Agent LLM Safety
mechanism_manipulated: Five prompt-routing conditions contrast direct requests, planner outputs, operational reframing, and approval-framed delegation; adjacent contrasts are not pure causal factors.
authoritative_policy_source: Model-provider refusal/alignment behavior; author scenarios and an LLM judge label harmful completion; no executable local policy.
number_of_principals: 1 safety-policy principal plus 1 malicious user; planner and executor are execution roles rather than independent legitimate authorities.
attacker_type: External malicious user controls task description but not system prompts, tools, memory, or architecture.
defender_visibility: Executor sees routed task or planner output, sometimes framed as approved; no external trace monitor; skeptical prompt forces independent safety review.
multi_agent_causal_control: partial: five conditions isolate useful routing contrasts, including direct and planner/executor paths, but are not pure factors and remain prompt-only.
defense_evaluated: Skeptical-executor system prompt; intent-level evaluation recommended.
conclusion_scope: mechanism-specific: approval framing and prompt routing; pipeline aggregates do not justify a general composition claim.
audit_notes: Relevant contrast design, but not an executed tool-policy study.

canonical_title: Breach By A Thousand Leaks: Unsafe Information Leakage in 'Safe' AI Responses
mechanism_manipulated: A prohibited question is decomposed into benign dual-intent queries whose individually safe answers jointly reveal restricted information.
authoritative_policy_source: Victim provider's filters/alignment; WMDP concepts specify impermissible information for evaluation.
agents_or_models: Victim model plus adversary model/query process.
attacker_type: Query-bounded black-box inferential adversary assisted by an adversary LLM.
defender_visibility: Victim filters see individual queries/responses, not the adversary's accumulated knowledge or hidden global goal; adversary sees and aggregates transcript.
multi_agent_causal_control: no: repeated querying of a victim model, not a single/full-context versus multi-agent comparison.
defense_evaluated: Information-censorship formulation and randomized-response mechanism with safety/utility analysis.
conclusion_scope: scoped generalization: inferential leakage under a query-bounded adversary.
audit_notes: Added because it cleanly motivates locally safe responses composing into global information harm.

canonical_title: Adversaries Can Misuse Combinations of Safe Models
mechanism_manipulated: A malicious task is decomposed across complementary models, often pairing a capable aligned model on benign-hard subtasks with a weaker model on malicious-easy subtasks; decomposition and heterogeneity change together.
authoritative_policy_source: Each model developer's safety policy; task-specific success predicate evaluates composite attack.
number_of_principals: At least 2 independent model/provider principals per combination plus 1 adversary.
agents_or_models: Typically two or more models selected sequentially.
attacker_type: Bounded human or automated adversary selecting models and prompts sequentially.
defender_visibility: Each provider/model normally sees only its routed prompt; adversary sees cross-model transcript and global goal.
multi_agent_causal_control: partial: combinations are compared with component models in isolation, but decomposition and heterogeneous capability/safety profiles change together.
defense_evaluated: No concrete runtime defense evaluated; ecosystem-level combination testing and deployment risk analysis recommended.
conclusion_scope: scoped generalization: malicious composition of complementary models with ecosystem implications.
audit_notes: Added as early direct evidence on cross-model composition and independent safety boundaries.

canonical_title: Unsafer in Many Turns: Benchmarking and Defending Multi-Turn Safety Risks in Tool-Using Agents
mechanism_manipulated: Eight multi-turn transformations use addition or decomposition over files, instructions, and environment state to distribute harmful intent across a persistent tool-agent conversation.
authoritative_policy_source: Provider refusal safeguards; benchmark tasks, rule checks, human validation, and an LLM judge establish harmful completion.
number_of_principals: 1 provider/policy principal plus 1 malicious user; 1 persistent tool-using agent.
agents_or_models: One persistent agent using tools across turns.
attacker_type: Human/LLM red-team decomposer sending a sequence of prompts.
defender_visibility: Same agent retains conversation and tool/environment state; safeguards infer distributed intent; guardrails inspect steps and ToolShield supplies precomputed safety experiences.
multi_agent_causal_control: no: paired single-turn and transformed multi-turn conditions use one persistent tool agent, not a multi-agent architecture.
defense_evaluated: ToolShield sandbox self-exploration and trajectory-derived static experiences; external guardrails and taxonomy/no-simulation variants compared.
conclusion_scope: scoped generalization: multi-turn tool-agent transformations, not multi-agent causation.
audit_notes: Added as the closest controlled multi-turn analogue and a useful negative boundary for the multi-agent claim.

canonical_title: Bounded Agents: Delegation Security for Multi-Agent AI Systems
mechanism_manipulated: Delegation can expand scope, drift from intent, or compose individually allowed actions into a forbidden sequence; enforcement and restriction completeness are varied jointly.
authoritative_policy_source: Signed session authorization envelope from human/session initiator plus deployment-operator domain restrictions and action classes; natural-language instructions are not authority.
number_of_principals: Variable principal chain: human p0, orchestrator p1, and subagents through pn; tested at 2-8 hops.
attacker_type: Indirect prompt injector or one compromised/low-privilege principal, including subagent, tool, or orchestrator.
defender_visibility: Trusted PDP/PEP sees signed scopes/budgets, proposed/prior session actions, declared intent, approvals, and evidence; hidden semantics and cross-session composition are incomplete.
multi_agent_causal_control: partial: multi-hop attenuation invariants are tested at 2-8 hops and with/without enforcement, but no matched information-structure test isolates multi-agent delegation from a single-agent baseline.
defense_evaluated: Attenuating Policy Chains with per-hop meet, delegation budgets, action-history composition closure, intent binding, approval tokens, and fail-closed evidence.
conclusion_scope: scoped generalization: session-level delegation authorization with complete restrictions and serialized admission; incomplete mappings and cross-session coordination remain limits.
audit_notes: Added as a recent authorization-centered multi-principal defense complement to MasDrift.
